title: Cosmic competition among created humanities
statement: Per the canon as the corpus organizes it, Earth's humanity is one of multiple humanities created by the Elohim on multiple worlds, each evaluated against the same maturity standard — the threshold coupling of woh-claim-0031 — with the outcome determining whether a humanity inherits its creators' level or destroys itself; the multi-world evaluation frame is canon-stated, and its competitive articulation is the corpus's organizing construct.

includes: The multi-world layer, canon-stated: the Elohim created humanities on other worlds; Earth's is not the only project
The evaluation layer: each humanity faces the maturity test woh-claim-0031 records for Earth's
The chain continuation: successful humanities become creators in turn (woh-claim-0030's forward direction)
The articulation disclosure: 'competition' as a frame is the corpus's; the canon states plurality and evaluation, not a contest between humanities
excludes: Inter-humanity contact or rivalry narratives; no such content is canon-stated
Population or location claims about the other humanities
Any ranking of Earth's standing; the corpus models no scoreboard
Fermi-paradox apologetics; the record does not deploy the frame to explain silence

source_references.locator: The multiple-worlds creation statements within the messages
The second message's development of the plurality and the evaluation standard

alternatives.statement: The multiple-humanities frame functions motivationally (the test is real because others have passed and failed); its content is exhortation, not cosmology.
'Competition' adds a contest the canon does not state; the corpus's articulation risks importing game-dynamics into an evaluation frame.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001, woh-claim-0030, or woh-claim-0031 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the plurality or evaluation statements.
Public prose begins narrating other humanities or deploying the frame for Fermi apologetics, both of which this record excludes.
